q: The main photosynthetic organs are the leaves. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Leaves are the primary photosynthetic organs in most plants.

q: Plants have extensive root systems above the ground. (2025-Set 4)
e: Plants have extensive root systems below the ground.

q: Glucose can be moved through the xylem as part of the sucrose molecule. (2024-Set 2)
e: Sucrose is transported through the phloem tissue, not the xylem.

q: Plants make their own organic molecules, using the process of respiration. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Plants produce organic molecules through the process of photosynthesis, not respiration.

q: Phloem transports water and inorganic ions from the roots to all parts of the plant. (2025-Set 11)
e: Xylem tissue transports water and inorganic ions from the roots to the rest of the plant.

q: Xylem tissue contains dead, empty hollow cells with end walls. (2025-Set7)
e: Xylem vessel elements are hollow, dead cells without end walls, forming continuous tubes.

q: Phloem tissue contains cells called mesophyll. (2024-Set 3)
e: Mesophyll cells are found in leaves, whereas phloem consists of sieve tube elements and companion cells.

q: Dissolved mineral ions are transported in the phloem tissue. (2025-Set 2)
e: Dissolved mineral ions are transported through the xylem tissue.

q: The dissolved organic compounds are transported in the xylem tissue. (2025-Set 10)
e: Dissolved organic compounds are transported through the phloem tissue during translocation.

q: In passive absorption, water moves through the symplast of the root. (2025-Set 13)
e: In passive absorption, water moves predominantly along the apoplastic pathway.

q: The symplast path includes the cell wall and intercellular spaces. (2025-Set 9)
e: The apoplastic path consists of cell walls and intercellular spaces.

q: The movement of water in the apoplastic pathway is slower than the symplastic pathway. (2025-Set 8)
e: Water moves faster through the apoplastic pathway because it encounters less resistance.

q: In most plants, stomata close during the day and open at night. (2025-Set 3)
e: In most plants, stomata open during the day to allow carbon dioxide entry and close at night.

q: In hot conditions, photosynthesis plays an important role in cooling the leaves. (2025-Set 1)
e: Transpiration plays a key role in cooling leaves through evaporative water loss.

q: Most transpiration takes place through the stomata. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းဒေသကြီးအများတွင်မေး)
e: The majority of water loss in transpiration occurs through the stomatal pores.

q: Transpiration helps the shape and structure of plant parts by keeping cells turgid. (2025-Set 6)
e: Maintaining water uptake via transpiration keeps plant cells turgid, providing structural support.

q: Transpiration supplies water for photosynthesis. (2025-Set 13)
e: The transpiration stream carries water continuously up to leaf cells for use in photosynthesis.

q: When leaves photosynthesize, they produce carbohydrates. (2024-Set 4)
e: Photosynthesis synthesizes simple carbohydrates (like glucose) using light energy.

q: The phloem tissue is a simple tissue. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား / 2025-Set 5 / 2026-Set 1)
e: Phloem is a complex tissue composed of multiple cell types.

q: Transpiration is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant. (2025-Set 12)
e: Translocation refers to the movement of dissolved organic substances through a plant.

q: Double circulatory system is found in birds and mammals. (2025-Set 7)
e: Birds and mammals possess a double circulatory system with separate pulmonary and systemic loops.

q: Birds and mammals need much more oxygen than fish. (2025-Set 10)
e: Birds and mammals are endothermic and require high metabolic rates, demanding more oxygen.

q: The open circulatory system is found in most arthropods. (2024-Set 2)
e: Most arthropods possess an open circulatory system where hemolymph bathes organs directly.

q: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is much thinner than that of the right. (2026-Set 2)
e: The wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than the right to pump blood throughout the systemic circulation.

q: The walls of the atria are thicker than those of the ventricles. (2025-Set 2)
e: Ventricles have significantly thicker muscular walls than atria.

q: The left atrioventricular valve is called bicuspid valve. (2025-Set 8)
e: The valve located between the left atrium and left ventricle is the bicuspid (mitral) valve.

q: The muscular wall of the right ventricle is much thicker than that of the left. (2024-Set 4)
e: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is thicker than that of the right ventricle.

q: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta into the foetus. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: The umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus.

q: Veins carry blood away from the heart towards the cells of the body. (2025-Set 11)
e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry blood toward the heart.

q: Almost all arteries carry deoxygenated blood. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းဒေသကြီးအများတွင်မေး)
e: Almost all arteries carry oxygenated blood (with the pulmonary artery being the exception).

q: The walls of the capillaries are very thick and contain elastic fibers. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Capillary walls are extremely thin (one cell layer thick) and lack elastic fibers.

q: Mature erythrocytes do not contain a nucleus. (2026-Set 1)
e: Mature red blood cells lack a nucleus to maximize space for hemoglobin.

q: Over 50% of the blood volume in the body is plasma. (2025-Set 3)
e: Plasma accounts for roughly 55% of total blood volume.

q: The erythrocytes transport oxygen from the lungs to all the cells. (2025-Set 2)
e: Erythrocytes transport oxygen from lungs to body cells, but specific textbook phrasing restricts this statement's absolute framing.

q: Platelets are tiny fragments of large cells called megakaryocytes. (2024-Set 3)
e: Platelets are non-cellular cell fragments derived from megakaryocytes.

q: Serotonin causes the smooth muscle of the blood vessel to contract. (2025-Set 6, 9)
e: Serotonin promotes vasoconstriction by causing vascular smooth muscles to contract.

q: Plasma, blood cells and platelets flow from a cut vessels. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: When a blood vessel is cut, blood components including plasma, cells, and platelets flow out.

q: Systole can be divided into atrial systole and ventricular systole. (2025-Set 12)
e: The contraction phase (systole) consists of sequential atrial contraction and ventricular contraction.

q: Cardiac muscle cells are myogenic. (2025-Set 5)
e: Cardiac muscle contractions originate within the muscle cells themselves without external nerve stimulation.

q: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by diffusion. (2025-Set 7)
e: Most water reenters venous capillaries via osmosis due to blood colloid osmotic pressure.
